subject: Vulnerability management evidence request — scan cadence & CVE remediation attestation
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acme.com
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Vulnerability management evidence request — Acme SOC 2

Hi Rachel / team,

We're kicking off the evidence collection for Acme's SOC 2 review and need to validate Redwood's vulnerability management controls. Can you provide the following items by EOD Wednesday (our auditors are on a tight timeline):

- Scan cadence (internal authenticated, external unauthenticated, SCA in CI)
- SLA definitions for remediation by severity (Critical / High / Medium / Low) and the escalation process
- An attestation (signed) that all Critical CVEs identified in the last 90 days were remediated or mitigated, with ticket references and remediation dates
- Most recent external scan summary (redacted is fine) and any open high/critical tickets with planned remediation dates

If you have a pre-packaged evidence bundle for vulnerability management that you can share, that would be ideal.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Senior InfoSec Manager, Acme Inc.
security@acme.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 10:02:14 -0800
Subject: Re: Vulnerability management evidence request — Acme SOC 2

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the heads up. I'm gathering the artifacts now and can provide a consolidated package, including a signed attestation. High-level answers below; we'll attach detail and artifacts in a follow-up by EOD.

- Scan cadence: internal authenticated scans run weekly (Nessus); external unauthenticated scans run monthly (Qualys); SCA (software composition analysis) runs on every PR in CI (Snyk + dependabot alerts).
- SLA (targeted): Critical = 48 hours from discovery to remediation or documented mitigation; High = 7 calendar days; Medium = 30 calendar days; Low = triaged per release window. Exceptions are documented via the security exceptions process (I can include the exception log).
- Attestation: we can provide a signed attestation covering remediation of Critical CVEs in the last 90 days with ticket IDs and dates.
- External scan summary: will attach the latest redacted PDF.

Looping in Dev for the remediation log and ticket references. We'll send a zip with the scan summary, remediation CSV, and the signed attestation.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Adding technical detail and the evidence filenames below. Attached: vuln_scan_summary_20251031.pdf (external scan summary), CVE_remediation_log_2025Q3.csv (export from our remediation tracker).

Technical details:
- Tools:
  - External scanning: Qualys (monthly unauthenticated + targeted authenticated for perimeter assets where applicable)
  - Internal authenticated scanning: Nessus Enterprise (weekly) with credentials for host-level checks
  - SCA/Dependency scanning: Snyk + dependabot (every PR), also runtime image scanning in our build pipeline
  - Container/runtime CVE monitoring: Clair & Trivy in staging and production image scans nightly
- Vulnerability intake & tracking: All findings that meet our severity threshold are triaged into the SEC backlog (Jira project: SEC). Each finding becomes a remediation ticket with priority and SLA fields.
- SLA enforcement: Criticals auto-create a P1 incident and notify on-call; expected remediation or mitigations documented within 48 hours. We run weekly remediation sprints for High/Medium items and track progress in Jira.
- Verification: Patches are validated via regression test runs and canary rollouts; we maintain a remediation verification checklist per ticket.

Attachment stubs:
- vuln_scan_summary_20251031.pdf (external scan redacted summary)
- CVE_remediation_log_2025Q3.csv (ticket id, cve, severity, discovery_date, remediation_date, owner)

Happy to run through the log with your auditor if they'd like a short walkthrough.

— Dev Patel
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rachel/Dev — this is helpful. A few follow-ups:

- We need a signed PDF attestation that explicitly states Redwood's SLA for Critical CVEs and confirms that all Criticals in the last 90 days were remediated or mitigated (include ticket references). Can you have that signed by an approver (Head of Security or equivalent)?
- For verification: can you confirm how you test that a remediation actually resolved the CVE (e.g., re-scan, exploit checks, CVE-specific tests) and whether that verification is completed within the same SLA window or separately?
- Do you have an emergency rollback/mitigation plan if a remediation causes production regressions? If so, please include a short description or link to the runbook.
- Finally, please send the most recent external scan summary (redacted) if possible.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — our auditor would like the signed attestation and remediation CSV by COB.

Jordan

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Jordan — sending the requested package. Attached files: vuln_scan_summary_20251031.pdf, CVE_remediation_log_2025Q3.csv, vuln_mgmt_attestation_20251112_signed.pdf (signed by our Head of Security).

Answers to your follow-ups:
- Attestation: the PDF is signed by Markus Klein (Head of Security). It states our SLA for Criticals = 48 hours and confirms remediation/mitigations for Critical CVEs discovered in the last 90 days, with ticket references included in the remediation CSV.
- Verification: we validate remediations by re-scanning affected assets and running targeted exploit/POC checks where available; verification entry (verify_date + verifier) is recorded on each Jira ticket. Verification is typically completed as part of the remediation workflow and is expected within the SLA window for Criticals; for High/Medium it is done during verification sprints (documented on ticket).
- Emergency mitigation/rollback: we maintain a production rollback/runbook (internal link) and an emergency mitigation checklist — small note: actual runbook is privileged, but we can provide the runbook title and a redacted outline for auditors.

Related links included: SOC 2 report (redacted) and the Jira search URL for open remediations. If your auditor wants a short walkthrough, Dev can join a 20–30 minute call tomorrow.

Thanks — I'll follow up if any auditor questions come back.

— Rachel Kim
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
